correctness.rationale: A cycle flow is path-constant with sum of path coefficients zero. Averaging a projection over within-path permutations and equal-length path exchanges does not increase its norm and preserves its range and identity action on the cycle space, so the minimization covers all linear projections. In path means the projection subtracts w times their sum, with w=(u,(1-u)/r,...). The two edge-column sums rule out u outside [0,1]. Inside, with R=b/a, the short-path sum is (1+R)(1-u), and the long-path sum has slope 1/R-(r-2)/r. The crossing, endpoint, and constant-long-column boundary give exactly the stated branches, including r=2. Euclidean least squares instead uses w proportional to reciprocal path lengths; the short-path column dominates, and symmetry gives the same infinity norm. Substitution of (a,b)=(2,2r) yields the family and exact ratio, including r=3 on the branch boundary where the norms are 4/3 and 2. The bundled finite checker was inspected, not executed; the analytic argument covers all parameters. The formulas agree when a=b, as expected from symmetry.
